question: A man purchases two fans for Rs. 2160. By selling one fan at a profit of 15% and the other at a loss of 9% he neither gains nor losses in the whole transaction. Find the cost price of each fan.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 'no profit, no loss' transaction, the ratio of their Cost Prices is inversely proportional to their respective profit and loss percentages.

Ratio of CP₁ to CP₂ = Loss% : Profit% = 9 : 15 = 3 : 5

Total ratio parts = 3 + 5 = 8 parts ⇒ 8 parts = Rs. 2160

1 part = 2160 ÷ 8 = Rs. 270

CP of 1st fan = 3 parts × 270 = Rs. 810, and CP of 2nd fan = 5 parts × 270 = Rs. 1350

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 810 & Rs. 1350.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total CP of two fans = Rs. 2160

Profit on the first fan = 15%

Loss on the second fan = 9%

Net result = Neither profit nor loss

**Calculations:**

Let the CP of the first fan be x.

Then, the CP of the second fan is (2160 − x).

In a 'no profit no loss' transaction, Profit amount on the 1st fan = Loss amount on the 2nd fan

⇒ 15% of x = 9% of (2160 − x)

⇒ (15 ÷ 100) × x = (9 ÷ 100) × (2160 − x)

⇒ 15x = 9 × (2160 − x)

⇒ 15x = 19440 − 9x

⇒ 15x + 9x = 19440

⇒ 24x = 19440

⇒ x = 19440 ÷ 24 = 810

So, the Cost Price of the first fan = Rs. 810

Cost Price of the second fan = 2160 − 810 = Rs. 1350

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 810 & Rs. 1350.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overall Profit/Loss % (Same Selling Price)

If two articles are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss given by (x ÷ 10)² %.

No Profit No Loss Condition

When the overall transaction results in neither profit nor loss, the absolute profit earned on the first item exactly cancels out the absolute loss incurred on the second item, giving the equation: CP₁ × Profit% = CP₂ × Loss%.
